chapter: Left out of the jazz books; Tatum, Handy and family
title: Studio work versus playing jazz in clubs
summary: Collins enjoys studio work, but Willard cites Shelly Manne and Ray Brown on losing jazz facility, and he says playing nightly with Troup was his outlet.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: Do you find it stifling to do studio work?

I enjoy it. Well, I enjoy the musicianship that's involved. You understand what I mean? It's an accomplishment. I mean, like when you do shows you never know what you have to play, and it's a sense of accomplishment, you know, to do these things. I enjoy it because it -- you have to be a good, thorough musician.
I know that you'd be very good --
Yeah, so this I enjoy, and an aside from that, it's good for you know your appetite. You make a little
But there are so many good jazz musicians out here in California particularly who are in the studios.

Shelly Manne Charlie Mann said he enjoys it up to a point, and then he finds it frustrating and maddening because he needs to stretch out and really play jazz. And if he takes all the studio calls he gets, there's not much time left to play jazz and he almost forgets how. Ray Brown has said that --
Well, Ray does an awful lot of playing other than for that show.

Now he does but (inaudible) that for awhile Ray was doing all studio work, and not any live playing. And he said that he'd forgotten how. He would hear things and think things he wanted to play but he couldn't make his fingers respond until he played for a couple weeks.

Yeah. Well, you just shouldn't take everything that's thrown at you, you know, you shouldn't take it. You should do a little of both, you know, you should get out and play in clubs. The best thing that happened to me, really, was when I went with Bobby Troup. Because as I told you before he was a stand up singer and he would go out of his club and leave me there and I got a chance to play at 2nd to the woodshed, and everybody came in to play. So it was very good.
In the meantime, I was doing quite a bit of recording and TV work, but I had this outlet. At night I would go and really play.
